taskPreset.title: Create Add Community Task
taskPreset.description: Author a complete HagiTask Community Task package from a structured brief, validate it locally, and open a Pull Request from your GitHub fork.

panel.contextSectionDescription: Choose where the task runs and which read-only material the executor may consult.
panel.briefSectionDescription: Everything below is written into the generated package. Vague input produces a vague task.
panel.projectHint: The authoring task will be created in the selected project. Its working directory is only scratch space for the fork checkout.
panel.taskNameHint: Human readable name of the task you are authoring. The canonical lowercase kebab-case task id is derived from it and can never be renamed later.
panel.repositoryAccessHint: Optionally attach repositories as read-only reference. Package files are always written to your Community Packages fork, never to these repositories.
panel.repositoryAccessEmpty: No repositories are available for the selected project yet.
panel.referenceVaultsHint: Optionally attach vaults as read-only reference context for specs, notes, or prior explorations.
panel.vaultEmptyDescription: Create a vault first if you want to attach reference material to this authoring run.
panel.projectReferencesHint: Optionally attach other projects as read-only context when the new task mirrors an existing workflow.
panel.objectiveHint: What the new Community Task does, who installs it, and which problem it removes.
panel.objectivePlaceholder: Keep API reference docs aligned with the current route handlers, so reviewers stop catching stale endpoint docs during code review.
panel.inputsHint: The panel fields the new task should collect, which are required, and the boundaries the executor must respect.
panel.inputsPlaceholder: Required: docs directory, source route directory. Optional: excluded paths. Repository access must stay explicit and default to read.
panel.qualityHint: How the new task must behave: write scope, non-interactive rules, tools it may use, and what it must never do.
panel.qualityPlaceholder: Run non-interactively, only edit files under the docs directory, never invent endpoints that are absent from the source, and report the real result of the docs build.
panel.acceptanceHint: Observable conditions that decide whether a run of the new task succeeded.
panel.acceptancePlaceholder: Every documented endpoint exists in source, every new endpoint is documented, and the docs build exits zero.
panel.publicationHint: Optional. Catalog, tags, best fit, and anything the store page should say.
panel.publicationPlaceholder: catalog: documentation; tags: api, docs, maintenance; best fit: teams with hand-written API references.

errors.missingRequiredFields: Fill in the task name, objective, input constraints, quality requirements, and acceptance criteria before submitting.
errors.ghNotAvailable: The GitHub CLI (gh) is required. Install it and run gh auth login before dispatching this task.
errors.ghNotAuthenticated: gh is not authenticated. Run gh auth login, then dispatch the task again.
errors.forkUnavailable: Your account cannot fork the upstream Community Packages repository. Check organization policy or repository permissions.
errors.validationFailed: Package validation failed. Fix the reported file, field, or rule error in the package source instead of editing generated output.
errors.pullRequestFailed: The pull request could not be created. The working branch was pushed to your fork, so you can open the pull request manually.
